statement: Under inference, the order in which predictors are listed in a least-squares model does not change the exposure's coefficient, interval or p-value (only sequential sums of squares depend on order, and the app does not report them), so the app does not ask about predictor order.
decision: order of predictors in the model
claimed_basis: Invariance of the least-squares solution to column permutation.

statement: For internal validation at typical clinical sample sizes, bootstrap optimism correction is the recommended default, repeated cross-validation is acceptable, and a single train/test split is the weakest option.
decision: the validation scheme's order on the seal card

statement: In a randomized trial, covariate adjustment only sharpens precision and causal wording is allowed; a case-control sample cannot give prevalence or absolute risk; matched sets are analyzed within each set; an observational study adjusts for confounders and speaks of associations.
decision: the design question, which gates adjustment and claim wording
claimed_basis: none stated (the drawer cites STROBE-nut only for naming the design)

statement: Under Predict, the cross-validated R² for a regression outcome is best reported as the squared Pearson correlation between the out-of-fold predictions and the outcomes, because it penalizes predictions that are systematically too high or too low and so is the conservative choice over 1 − SSE/SST.
regime: regression outcome under prediction, cross-validated or held-out scoring

statement: Before the lock under Estimate, the share of rows an exclusion rule (an energy-intake screen) removes, multiplied by the largest standardized mean difference (Austin 2009; pooled-SD for numbers, per-level proportion difference for categories) between the removed and kept rows on the adjustment set, is an outcome-blind predictor of how far keeping every row would move the exposure's estimate in units of its 95% interval half-width, good enough to band the noticing as doesn't change / could bias / act on it.
regime: Dietary lens; Estimate or Describe; an energy screen (Goldberg, or a range rule on the energy column) among the exclusions; before the plan's lock
decision: Predicted band and recommended triage disposition of the implausible-reporters noticing
claimed_basis: SURFACING_POLICY §2.3 item 2 (design-space movement, 'rows lost × max |SMD|', the shared-missingness-mechanism rank signal); Austin 2009 for SMD; 9 calibration cases in materiality_calibration.json

statement: The within-strata residual with total energy kept in the outcome model has the standard model's estimand: its nutrient coefficient is the standard model's exactly, because the residual and total energy span the same model as the nutrient and total energy.
regime: residual method with strata (e.g. within sex) and total energy kept
decision: estimand sentence and row meanings shown for the stratified residual
claimed_basis: none specific to strata (inherits McCullough & Byrd 2023 from the pooled residual)

statement: For a yes/no outcome, a held-out validation set with at least 10 events estimates the C-statistic and the calibration slope precisely enough to be useful, so a held-out score is offered from 10 events.
decision: minimum size of a held-out set

statement: A column named like an identifier is not a unit identifier (and clustering intervals by it is invalid) when it holds fewer than 3 distinct values, or at most 10 repeating word labels without digits (e.g., a case-control `patient` 0/1, `respondent` Self/Proxy, `person` mother/father); 3-10 repeating coded values may be a small study's units or a group code and are asked; more than 10 repeating values, or one value per row, is a unit structure.
regime: Any table; columns whose names read as identifiers.
decision: Identifier role confidence and whether it may cluster intervals or group the seal.
claimed_basis: BLUEPRINT §14 rule 1: "An identifier has at least 3 distinct values and a unit structure." (gate: `participant` coded yes/no clustered intervals by 2 values, so no interval was reported); FEW_UNITS = CATEGORY_LEVELS 10 (recognizers.py:1412-1425).

statement: Complete-case analysis gives unbiased regression coefficients if and only if whether a value is missing does not depend on the outcome, given the predictors.
regime: inference; complete-case analysis of a regression (linear, logistic, Cox, etc.) with missing predictors
decision: complete-cases option (available, ranked second under inference); its stated assumption in the record and methods sentence; the row-loss concern

statement: A feature whose D-ratio (pooled-QC SD over the study samples' SD) is 50% or more carries too little biological variance relative to technical variance and is removed, with the QC SD frozen before the seal and the study SD taken from each training fold.
regime: metabolomics; pooled-QC answer variant with D-ratio chosen
claimed_basis: Broadhurst et al. 2018: 'the acceptance criterion for D-ratio is set to, at most, < 50%'.

statement: For a least-squares estimate on an outcome with a clinical cut-off c, writing y = min(y, c) + max(y − c, 0) splits the coefficient exactly into a part from values above the cut and a part from values below, which add to the primary's coefficient, and the estimate is 'mostly the tail' when the part above is more than half and its interval excludes zero.
regime: inference; linear model; outcome with a clinical cut-off
decision: the 'typical person, or the tail?' standing question
claimed_basis: linearity of least squares in y (no source)

statement: From an effective size of 300, a seeded quasi-random search (scrambled Sobol) of 8 candidates, 16 from an effective size of 1,000, plus the standard settings, each scored by nested inner cross-validation, is enough to choose settings that predict at least as well as the standard settings, because the declared search spaces have low effective dimension, where random search is a strong baseline.
regime: prediction; searched families (boosted trees, XGBoost, forest); n_plan >= 300
decision: tuning plan: number of Sobol candidates S (8 / 16; halved under 'lighter')
claimed_basis: RECIPES §4.2 'The strategy in v2' reason 3: random search is 'a surprisingly strong baseline' (Bischl et al. 2023; Bergstra & Bengio 2012); reasons 1-2 are replay and a known budget, not accuracy.

statement: For a yes/no outcome, resampling (SMOTE, over- or undersampling) or class weighting should not be applied by default, because it overestimates the rarer class's probability without raising the AUC; a decision should move the threshold instead.
decision: no resampling or class weighting by default; the sentence beside every binary fit
claimed_basis: van den Goorbergh et al., JAMIA 2022;29:1525 (quoted).
